title: ms-to-revenue narrative: latency -> unit-econ field draft
content:
Objective:
- Build a short narrative that ties median and tail latency improvements to concrete revenue and cost outcomes for realistic customer workloads.
- Create 2–3 customer-facing claim lines plus a short internal playbook on what data/proofs to surface in demos, sales cycles, and case studies.

Quick executive claim candidates (need validation):
- "Shave 100−200ms off median generation time for interactive apps — netting 1.5–3× higher user throughput and lower token cost per active session."
- "Sub-100ms median for 128–512 token prompts at production scale (hosted + dedicated), with fallbacks that protect tail latency."
- "Cut per-conversation inference spend by up to 40% via smart batching + prefix caching without degrading response quality."

Why this narrative? (core links in the story)
- Customers buy value, rarely raw ms. Translate latency to: increased concurrent users, lower infra spend, higher retention via faster UX.
- Unit-econ path: fewer costly retries, higher session density per GPU, lower per-request queuing overhead.

Field math (back-of-envelope examples — flag for benching):
- Baseline example (customer A): chat app, avg prompt 150 tokens, reply 120 tokens, 60k requests/day.
  - Baseline median latency 220ms, p95 1.1s. Server utilization requires 8 GPUs to meet SLAs.
  - After optimizations (kernel selection + KV cache + batching): median 95ms, p95 420ms. Effective throughput per GPU increases ~2.6×.
  - Implication: same traffic can be served with 3 GPUs (instead of 8) -> ~62.5% infrastructure cost reduction for inference.
  - If infra was 60% of total inference spend, overall inference line item drops ~37%.

- Batching and amortization example (session amortization):
  - When we compress 1k short requests into 250 batched token operations (via continuous batching), average tokens processed per request drops due to shared KV and prefix reuse.
  - For workloads with repeated contexts (FAQ/chatbots), prefix caching reduces decoded tokens by ~12–30% depending on reuse pattern.

What proof artifacts we should prepare (priority order):
1) Bench harness w/ 3 realistic workload traces (customer-provided dummy traces + synthetic): short-chat (20–256 tokens), assistant (200–800 tokens), summarization (800–2k tokens). Include p50/p95/p99 and cost/GPU curves.
2) Microbench: kernel selection table showing runtime delta by sequence length and quantization profile.
3) Case simulation: scaled cluster simulation showing GPU-count vs QPS and token cost for baseline vs optimized.
4) Customer-friendly charts: ms -> active users mapping, cost per 1k requests bar chart, and a short animation for demos (before/after).

Competitive framing notes (quick scan, validate with research):
- Cloud vendor X: straightforward instance pricing; often only vertical scaling -> harder to show per-token savings because they sell raw GPUs. Their message = "standardized capacity" not inference economics.
- Provider Y: emphasizes model quality and breadth. Their latency story is mostly single-node latency numbers without amortization/production batching context.
- Open-source self-hosting: cheaper on paper but requires engineering ops to get similar batching/caching and routing policies. Use this to position Redwood: "same openness, built production ops".

Suggested messaging levers (how to say faster/cheaper without being overly prescriptive):
- Speed-as-business-metric: "Reduce time-to-response to increase concurrent active sessions per server"
- Cost-as-impact: "Lower inference unit cost via smarter execution (batching, cache, quantization guidance)"
- Reliability tie-in: "Graceful degradation keeps apps live during bursts — preserving revenue even under load"
- Phrasing samples for sales scripts:
  - "If we can shave your median generation from ~200ms to under 100ms, you can support 2–3× more concurrent users on the same capacity — that typically means meaningfully lower infra spend or a lower latency SLA for your top customers."
  - "We measure at the token and session level; we can show you exactly how a specific route or workflow will change the inference bill. We'll run a 7–14 day proof with your trace and a model recommendation."

Experiments to run (short plan):
- Phase 0 (1 week): Re-run benchmarks for three representative models and quantization profiles; collect p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens at 1–10k QPS.
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Customer trace injection — run side-by-side: customer-hosted baseline vs Redwood optimized stack (identical model weights) to surface end-to-end infra delta.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): Small pilot with canary traffic for a customer route (A/B) measuring retention and click-through differences tied to response latency.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need a standard conversion formula: ms -> concurrent users -> GPU count -> $ saved. Who owns the cluster-sim script? (ask infra eng, @Mark)
- Validate prefix-caching savings across model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder). Riya to help scope.
- Legal check on phrasing for outbound claims (percent reductions) — get approvals before fielding in sales assets.

Appendix: short demo script (sales)
- Slide 1: Problem — "Slow responses cost you users & money" (2 bullets + quick customer stat)
- Slide 2: Our approach — "runtime + routing + caching + metrics" (1-liner for each)
- Slide 3: Proof snapshot — before/after p50/p95 + GPU count -> cost table (one slide)
- Slide 4: Ask — "Run a quick 7-day trace proof. We’ll show you expected savings and latency map."

Notes on style & approvals:
- Keep external claims conservative: prefer ranges ("up to X%", "typically X–Y×") and back with a footnote pointing to bench artifact.
- Create a canonical GTM bench report (hosted under the Confluence link above) that sales can reference in deal decks.

Unresolved phrasing experiments (brainstorm):
- "ms-to-revenue" vs "ms-to-throughput" — which resonates more with CRO? Test both in field outreach.
- Instead of "cheaper", test "lower cost-per-active-user" in customer conversations — more outcome-focused.

Next actions (this week):
- Riya: collect the three customer traces we can anonymize for the bench. (due 2025-02-18)
- Mark: spin a quick cluster sim and share GPU vs QPS baseline (due 2025-02-21)
- Noah: draft 2 short sales scripts with different phrasings (ms-to-revenue / cost-per-active-user) for A/B phone calls (due 2025-02-24)
- Sofia (me): tie the bench outputs to one short visual and a 1‑pager claim sheet for the field (due 2025-03-03)

Scratch notes / fragments to keep in doc history:
- "If we don't own the model, we own the serving economics" — hero line to test in leadership comms.
- Slack refs: #g2m-performance thread (see thread 2025-02-10)
- Related assets: see linked PR and confluence page for raw outputs.

-- end draft --

(Informal: this is intentionally rough — mix of math, sketchy assumptions, and a list of what to build next. Want to keep it lightweight for quick iteration with sales and infra.)
